subject: Climate & Environment
title: Fossil Fuels and CO₂
description: Learn Fossil Fuels and CO₂ in one minute.

hook.text: In 1882, Thomas Edison opened the first coal power plant. The carbon age had begun.

buildup.text: Coal, oil, and natural gas now supply about 80% of the world's energy.

discovery.text: Burning them releases carbon that was locked underground for 300 million years.

twist.text: We burn over 36 billion tons of CO₂ into the air each year — and it keeps rising.

climax.text: Nature absorbs about half. The rest accumulates in the atmosphere year after year.

punchline.text: We are digging up ancient sunlight and turning it into heat.

quiz.question: What percentage of global energy comes from fossil fuels today?

details.summary: Burning fossil fuels for energy, transport, and industry is responsible for roughly 75 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions. Coal, oil, and natural gas release CO2 that had been locked underground for millions of years, fundamentally altering the atmosphere's composition.
details.whyItMatters: Fossil fuel combustion is the single largest driver of climate change. Decarbonizing the energy system is the most consequential transformation humanity must undertake.
takeaways: Fossil fuels account for about 75 percent of global GHG emissions
Coal emits roughly twice the CO2 per unit of energy compared to gas
Roughly 80 percent of known reserves must stay unburned to limit warming to 1.5 degrees

faq.question: How much of global energy still comes from fossil fuels?
faq.answer: Fossil fuels provided roughly 80 percent of global primary energy as of 2023, down only slightly from 85 percent two decades earlier. Despite rapid renewable growth, fossil fuel use in absolute terms continues to rise in many regions.

faq.question: What is the concept of stranded assets in fossil fuels?
faq.answer: Limiting warming to 1.5 degrees requires leaving roughly 80 percent of known fossil fuel reserves in the ground. The value of these unburnable reserves, estimated at trillions of dollars, becomes stranded assets for companies and nations.
